To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed a framework to assess coral reef resilience and applied it to a MPA in the Mexican Caribbean to identify local-scale stressors and potential adaptive management actions to improve resilience of coral reefs.

we applied the Maynard et al. (Coral Reefs 29: 381-391, 201010) resilience index framework, which uses a suite of indicators to rank the resilience of coral reefs, to the Parque Nacional Arrecife de Puerto Morelos (Mexico) and identified stressors that can be influenced through management actions to promote coral reef resilience.
we applied a coral reef resilience index to a MPA in the Mexican Caribbean, which identified management priorities to promote reef resilience.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of a resilience framework that is useful to managers in the Caribbean and beyond to promote resilience in their MPAs.
the development of an effective and practical tool to promote resilience in MPAs, and to provide a framework for managers to make informed and effective decisions.
developing methods to translate monitoring results into management actions to promote reef resilience.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this study demonstrates the value of a monitoring program to provide information that can guide management decisions to improve the resilience of coral reefs and thus promote ecosystem health.
a resilience index can be a useful management tool to identify management needs for MPAs, and that this tool should be applied more widely in coral reef MPAs.

the resilience index framework developed by Maynard et al. (Coral reefs 29:381-391, 2011) is a useful tool for MPA managers to identify the relative resilience of coral reefs and to guide adaptive management actions that can promote resilience.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PNAPM has high potential to promote resilience, but that management actions are needed to realize this potential.
the resilience framework is useful for managers and that it is important to have a management plan in place to guide adaptive management actions.
the resilience index framework can help MPA managers identify and prioritize actions to promote resilience.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the resilience index is a useful framework to identify management actions to promote coral reef resilience.
a comprehensive resilience assessment can provide a useful framework for managers to evaluate their management actions and to make decisions that will promote resilience.

monitoring data can be assimilated into a resilience index framework that is applicable to a wide variety of coral reef ecosystems to provide managers with a comprehensive understanding of local stressors and management actions needed to promote resilience.
